title: Forces in Everyday Life
intro: Pushes, pulls, friction and Newton's laws discovered with ropes, rubber strips, shoes and handcarts.

lessons.title: Force: Pushes and Pulls Everywhere
lessons.focus: Force defined by what it does; hunt for ten forces in the compound (opening sufuria lid, pulling mkokoteni, wind on mabati).
lessons.advanced: Classify each found force as contact or non-contact; justify the classification of gravity.

lessons.title: What Forces Do: Move, Stop, Turn, Shape
lessons.focus: Four effects catalogued by kicking a ball, squeezing clay, bending a stick, stretching rubber.
lessons.advanced: A force changes shape but the object does not move: where does the work go? Preview elastic energy.

lessons.title: Measuring Force: The Newton and the Rubber-Strip Meter
lessons.focus: Build and calibrate a force meter from rubber strips using water (1 L ≈ 1 kg ≈ 10 N); the spring balance idea.
lessons.advanced: Your rubber strip stretches non-linearly. Describe a two-point calibration error and a fix using more calibration points.

lessons.title: Gravity: Earth's Pull on Everything
lessons.focus: Gravity as downward pull; falling mango vs thrown stone; weight as gravitational force; g ≈ 10 N/kg introduced.
lessons.advanced: Why doesn't the Moon fall onto Earth despite gravity? Seed the idea of orbital motion.

lessons.title: Weight = Mass × g: Getting It Right
lessons.focus: W = mg; measure masses with beam balance, weights with spring balance; tabulate and verify factor of 10.
lessons.advanced: A scale calibrated in Nairobi reads your 'weight' 60 kg. Is that reading mass or force, and what error appears at high altitude?

lessons.title: Balanced and Unbalanced Forces
lessons.focus: Tug-of-war with sisal rope; equal forces → no motion change; net force concept; stationary objects have balanced forces.
lessons.advanced: A 400 N pull left meets 350 N right: find net force and direction; describe the motion change.

lessons.title: Drawing Force Diagrams
lessons.focus: Arrows show size and direction; draw forces on a book on a desk, a hanging jerrican, a leaning ladder.
lessons.advanced: Draw the hanging jerrican diagram with the rope at 20°: which component carries the weight? Qualitative vectors.

lessons.title: Friction I: The Force That Opposes Sliding
lessons.focus: Rub hands, drag shoe on floor then grass; friction acts opposite motion; surface roughness matters.
lessons.advanced: Friction is caused by microscopic welds between surfaces: explain why polishing reduces it only up to a point.

lessons.title: Friction II: When We Need It
lessons.focus: Walking, tyre treads on murram, jembe handle grip, writing chalk, boda braking: life without friction skit.
lessons.advanced: Explain why wet murram roads reduce friction and how tread channels water away.

lessons.title: Friction III: Reducing It with Oil, Rollers and Bearings
lessons.focus: Grease on hinges, rollers under debe, ball bearings from boda hubs; sliding vs rolling compared by pull test.
lessons.advanced: Pull-force drops from 18 N to 3 N with rollers: compute friction reduction percentage and where the energy was going.

lessons.title: Friction Lab: Pull Tests on Surfaces
lessons.focus: Spring balance drags a loaded block over wood, sandpaper, grass, oiled wood; force vs load graph.
lessons.advanced: Plot friction vs load; find the gradient — introduce coefficient of friction μ for your surfaces.

lessons.title: Air Resistance: The Invisible Brake
lessons.focus: Flat vs crumpled paper drop; plastic-bag parachute; streamlining preview; drag grows with speed.
lessons.advanced: Why does a falling raindrop not accelerate forever? Introduce terminal velocity conceptually.

lessons.title: Water Resistance and Streamlining
lessons.focus: Sweep hand flat vs edge-on through water; fish and canoe shapes; mould clay hulls and drag-test them.
lessons.advanced: Explain in particle terms why water drag exceeds air drag at the same speed.

lessons.title: Tension: Forces in Ropes and Strings
lessons.focus: Sisal rope tension; tug-of-war revisited with force meter in the middle; knots and why they slip; clothesline sag.
lessons.advanced: A 50 N pull on each end of a rope — is the tension 50 N or 100 N? Resolve the classic misconception.

lessons.title: Compression and Support Forces
lessons.focus: Standing on soil vs mattress; pillars and poles; chalk under compression snaps differently; stool legs.
lessons.advanced: Why does chalk fail in tension before compression? Link to crack opening at the bent side.

lessons.title: The Normal Force: Surfaces Push Back
lessons.focus: Table pushes up on books; bathroom scale reads the push; leaning on a wall; normal means perpendicular.
lessons.advanced: On a 30° ramp, which is bigger: weight or normal force? Resolve vectors qualitatively.

lessons.title: Elastic Forces: Things That Spring Back
lessons.focus: Rubber, springs, bows: restoring force grows with stretch; preview Hooke's law; slingshot (manati) energy teaser.
lessons.advanced: Sketch force vs stretch for rubber: why does it curve up at large extension? (Polymer chains uncoiling.)

lessons.title: Forces Come in Pairs: A First Look at Reaction
lessons.focus: Push the wall, the wall pushes you; step off a floating log and it moves back; pair forces act on different bodies.
lessons.advanced: If pair forces are equal and opposite, why does anything accelerate? (They act on different objects.)

lessons.title: Newton's First Law: Inertia
lessons.focus: Coin on card flick; passengers lurch when matatu brakes; inertia depends on mass; seatbelt teaser.
lessons.advanced: Use inertia to explain why a fully loaded lorry needs a longer braking distance than an empty one at the same speed.

lessons.title: Newton's Second Law: F = ma
lessons.focus: Push empty then full debe with same effort; acceleration depends on force and mass; quantify with toy car and falling mass.
lessons.advanced: A 2 kg trolley accelerates at 1.5 m/s² under a hanging mass: compute the net force and discuss friction's role.

lessons.title: Newton's Third Law: Action and Reaction
lessons.focus: Balloon rocket on a string line; walking as pushing Earth back; rowing a canoe; identify pairs in five scenarios.
lessons.advanced: A 500 N boda accelerates forward: identify the action-reaction pair at the tyre-road contact.

lessons.title: Net Force and Acceleration Lab
lessons.focus: Falling-mass trolley on a smooth board; vary hanging mass; acceleration vs force graph through origin.
lessons.advanced: From a vs F graph gradient, extract the system mass; explain the intercept if friction was not fully compensated.

lessons.title: Combining Forces at Angles
lessons.focus: Two students pull one jerrican with ropes at an angle; resultant feels less than the sum; parallelogram idea by drawing.
lessons.advanced: Two 40 N pulls at 60° to each other: find the resultant by scale drawing; compare with 80 N straight pull.

lessons.title: Everyday Force Mysteries Clinic
lessons.focus: Why door handles sit far from hinges; opening paint tins with a panga edge; loosening tight bottle caps with cloth.
lessons.advanced: Explain the paint-tin lever with moments: tin-lid rim is fulcrum; compute MA for a 15 cm panga vs 2 cm lid lip.

lessons.title: Build: Balloon Rocket Line
lessons.focus: Straw + taut string + balloon; test balloon size, payload (paperclips), launch angle; measure travel distance.
lessons.advanced: Predict how payload mass affects final distance using F=ma and impulse reasoning; test it.

lessons.title: Unit Review: Force Detective Day
lessons.focus: Stations around school: identify, measure and draw forces (gate, flagpole, water tank, seesaw); unit quiz.
lessons.advanced: Design one station yourself with a measurable force question and a marking scheme.
